title: Where Is Everybody?
text: Westbrook Van Voorhis recorded the pilot's original narration. Serling later re-recorded it himself so the narration would be consistent with the rest of the series.

title: Where Is Everybody?
text: Unlike most episodes, which were made at MGM, the pilot was shot at Universal Studios, with the Courthouse Square set standing in for the town of Oakwood.

title: Where Is Everybody?
text: Before this pilot, CBS bought Serling's teleplay "The Time Element" and shelved it; it was later found in the vaults and aired on Westinghouse Desilu Playhouse on November 24, 1958.

title: The Encounter
text: Because of its racial overtones, the episode was kept out of US syndication until 2016.

title: Sounds and Silences
text: A writer sued Serling for plagiarism over this episode and won damages. Since the case was still going on when the syndication package was put together, the episode was held back until 1984.

title: Living Doll
text: Talky Tina was voiced, without credit, by June Foray, who also supplied the voice of Mattel's Chatty Cathy doll, the toy Tina was modeled on.

title: Living Doll
text: Although Charles Beaumont is credited, the script was ghostwritten by Jerry Sohl while Beaumont was too ill to write; Beaumont insisted on splitting the fee.

title: Living Doll
text: Toy Story 4 director Josh Cooley has said that Talky Tina inspired the film's doll Gabby Gabby.

title: Living Doll
text: The house seen in the episode was reused from the earlier episode "Ring-a-Ding Girl".

title: Queen of the Nile
text: Credited to Charles Beaumont, the episode was actually ghostwritten by Jerry Sohl as Beaumont's health declined.

title: Queen of the Nile
text: The shot of a victim crumbling to dust is recycled footage from the season 1 episode "Long Live Walter Jameson".

source.title: Queen of the Nile (The Twilight Zone) - Wikipedia

title: The New Exhibit
text: Charles Beaumont receives the writing credit, but Jerry Sohl ghostwrote the script because Beaumont's illness had left him unable to write.

title: Ninety Years Without Slumbering
text: George Clayton Johnson disliked how his story "Tick of Time" was rewritten, especially the new ending, so his on-screen credit appears under the pseudonym "Johnson Smith".

title: Ninety Years Without Slumbering
text: This was the last score Bernard Herrmann composed for the series.

title: The Masks
text: Director Ida Lupino was the only woman to direct an episode of The Twilight Zone.

title: The Sixteen-Millimeter Shrine
text: Star Ida Lupino later went behind the camera for the series, directing the season 5 episode "The Masks".

title: An Occurrence at Owl Creek Bridge
text: This is a French short film directed by Robert Enrico in 1961, bought and aired as a season 5 episode with an introduction by Serling. It won Best Short Subject at Cannes in 1962 and the Academy Award for Best Live Action Short Film in 1963.

title: Button, Button
text: Richard Matheson disliked this adaptation of his story, particularly its new ending, so the teleplay is credited to his pseudonym "Logan Swanson".

title: Button, Button
text: The same Matheson story was later adapted as Richard Kelly's 2009 film The Box, in which Basil Hoffman, the Steward here, plays a different role.

title: It's Still a Good Life
text: Bill Mumy and Cloris Leachman reprise their roles as Anthony and Agnes Fremont from the 1961 original. Anthony's daughter Audrey is played by Mumy's real-life daughter, Liliana Mumy.
